speakers: Scott Bessent (US Treasury Secretary, ex-Soros CIO, Key Square founder)
summary: Wilfried Frost interviews Treasury Secretary Bessent (recorded March 2026, during the Iran conflict) on his macro investing principles and on Treasury policy. Investing lessons: bet against consensus at turning points, stage catalysts (Japan yen 2011-13), keep risk modest. Policy views: bond market and functioning matter most, oil shock depends on duration, SPR release priced in early, tariffs rebuilt under Sections 301/122, BoE-style limited QE.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: when people panic is when they're you're not able to have price discovery, when markets close, when there's the threat of gating
claims.claim: Panic arises not from price moves but from loss of price discovery (closed markets, gating), so the policy priority is that markets keep functioning with buyers matched to sellers.
claims.testable: partly - episodes of market closure can be studied

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: You never want to have to sell at the bottom. You never want to find yourself like chasing at the top.
claims.claim: Know your own risk tolerance and do not get out over your skis, so you are never forced to sell at the bottom or chase at the top.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: the crowd is right 85 or 90% of the time and that's the momentum
claims.claim: The consensus is usually right and follows momentum, but the big money is made when things turn or when you can imagine an outcome different from consensus.
claims.direction: follow momentum, bet against consensus at turns

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: I'm always looking like how could the consensus be wrong?
claims.claim: Biggest successes came from taking the other side of elite opinion (ERM exit, US national housing decline, Japan escaping deflation); ask how the consensus framing could be wrong.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: the deepest, most liquid, and most most solid in the world
claims.claim: The US Treasury market is the most important market for policy; Treasury keeps it resilient through transparency and operational and settlement robustness and monitors it daily.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: can you imagine a different state of the world and then you're also trying to predict the when
claims.claim: A macro trade needs a vision of a different state of the world plus the timing (when, why, how) and the implementation, and it must be mispriced.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: the ability to put something back on the shelf
claims.claim: Guard against endowment bias (wanting to implement work already done): do immense research, then wait if timing is wrong, as with the yen before 2012.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: when the Japanese switched off the nuclear reactors, they had to start importing more fossil fuels, and it took the current account
claims.claim: After Fukushima Japan's nuclear shutdown forced fuel imports, turning a ~3% of GDP current account surplus into a deficit, an early catalyst for a weaker yen.
claims.conditions: when a persistent surplus turns to deficit
claims.testable: yes - current account and FX can be tested

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: I believe there were three board seats opening at the Bank of Japan
claims.claim: Decisive catalyst for the yen short: Abe's reflationary platform plus three open BoJ board seats let the Prime Minister reconstitute a deflationist board, including the governor.
claims.conditions: when political control of the central bank board changes

claims.speaker: Wilfried Frost
claims.quote: I have no idea, but it will be the market ride of a lifetime
claims.claim: Policy changes can drive huge price moves regardless of whether the policy works; as policymaker the speaker now judges what delivers rather than what is priced.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: they've done a fantastic job of restructuring the economy
claims.claim: Abenomics started as a market success and then became structural: shareholder rights, return on capital, womenomics, labor mobility.
claims.testable: partly - governance-reform effects on returns are testable

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: there is information value in the market sometimes
claims.claim: Even as a policymaker the market carries information; his past work was guessing what policymakers would do, now he asks what can, should and will be done and how the market will react.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: I don't think it it it's the the level. I think it's probably the duration.
claims.claim: What hurts the US economy about an oil spike is duration rather than level (2008 reached 147), and record US liquids production insulates household energy bills; WTI had gone from under 60 to a 114-115 peak.
claims.conditions: when the US is a net energy exporter
claims.testable: partly - duration-of-shock effect on growth is testable

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: The market lives in the future.
claims.claim: The oil spike reversed on the FT report of a 300-400 million barrel IEA release (the biggest one-day reversal in history), so the release was priced in before the official announcement.
claims.indicator: oil price reaction to SPR release news
claims.testable: partly - reaction to news vs official event can be studied

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: we know that they have not mined the straits
claims.claim: Hormuz tanker flow is expected to recover once US Navy or an international coalition can escort ships after air control, since the straits are not mined.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: Lloyd's does call force majeure and the policies drop away
claims.claim: A government-backed insurance product (DFC, $20bn) replaces private cover that Lloyd's withdraws under force majeure, so tankers can keep moving.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: that 11 billion is a lot of money, but you know, we we we have cushions built in
claims.claim: War cost (about $11bn after a couple of weeks) is not a fiscal constraint.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: US Treasuries had their best year since 2022
claims.claim: Foreign demand for Treasuries was increasing, with the 10-year the only G7 bond market with lower yields last year.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: those barrels are going to end up in China anyway
claims.claim: Sanctioning Russian barrels has little effect when the cargoes would reach China; a 30-day waiver for India uses barrels already on the water.
claims.indicator: Russian oil flows to India and China

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: I think this is a generational opportunity in the Western Hemisphere
claims.claim: Latin American governments are shifting from far left to centre-right and market-friendly, creating an opportunity for US alliances.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: I think the Fed is worried about maybe the energy component triggering inflationary expectations
claims.claim: The Fed's reaction to an oil shock depends on whether it lifts inflation expectations and on how long it slows growth: potential energy that can bounce back, or a permanent slowdown.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: a chance we can move to a substantially lower oil price regime the over the medium term
claims.claim: Once the Iran conflict is resolved in US favour, oil could move to a substantially lower regime than the pre-war level below $60.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: one of the things that got us the great inflation 22 and 23
claims.claim: Extraordinary measures should only occur in extraordinary times: the BoE stabilised gilts in spring 2020 and stepped back, whereas the Fed kept buying for years, which helped cause the 2022-23 inflation.
claims.testable: partly - QE duration and inflation can be analysed

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: how has banking regulation since the GFC affected the size of the balance sheet in terms of the interbank market
claims.claim: Shrinking the Fed balance sheet (or revaluing gold) needs advance signalling and a review of how post-GFC regulation raised the demand for reserves, versus a skinnier-reserve model where banks lend to each other.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: there's nothing that tells me that shadow shadow banking is having a systemic problem
claims.claim: Private credit wobbles are a shadow banking issue; Treasury monitors linkages to regulated banks and insurers but sees no systemic problem.
claims.testable: partly - bank-private credit links are measurable

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: The Supreme Court uh ruled that the president does not have the ability to use IEPA
claims.claim: After the Supreme Court bars IEEPA tariffs, the administration rebuilds the tariff wall under Section 301 (challenged over 4,000 times) and a 150-day Section 122 tariff, now a global 10%, with trade deals kept.
claims.testable: partly - tariff rate changes and market reaction can be studied

claims.speaker: Wilfried Frost
claims.quote: spoken about how you have to earn the right to be able to take risk. You have to stay in the game.
claims.claim: Buffett's rules (don't lose money; don't forget rule one) and chip-stack logic: the risk you take depends on how big your stack is.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: I think we we have this leadership. We have an energy dominance.
claims.claim: US relative strength rests on energy dominance (an exporter, not an importer), technology lead and a rebuilt military.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: we're going to have over 70 or 80% of all the compute in the world up from 40 or 50 a few years ago
claims.claim: The US AI boom lifts its share of global compute to 70-80% (from 40-50%) and US growth should return to 3% versus 0.3% celebrated in the EU after the conflict.
claims.indicator: US share of world compute, US GDP growth
claims.testable: partly - compute share and growth are measurable

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: debt to GDP is higher everywhere in the world
claims.claim: Debt-to-GDP rose everywhere after the GFC and COVID, so the US is in better relative shape.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: You you think about scenarios and then can you prove it?
claims.claim: Investing combines quantitative work and a qualitative narrative: build scenarios and then test whether they can be proved.
